budgets.name: Duplicate
budgets.measure: Requests the github-projects plugin sends to GitHub for one image a copy carries that the destination record does not yet hold: the upload and the authenticated read that verifies it, beyond the requests the same copy sends without the image.
budgets.inner_measure_reason: Headroom on the shared board token is the measure of record and no check may reach the live board or its token, so it is counted at a loopback GitHub endpoint through the real binary.
budgets.workload: A document copy carrying 6 new images, and a task copy carrying 2, into a github-projects source pointed at the loopback endpoint; the repository-id read is counted once per source instance and excluded from the per-image figure. Each image is a PNG generated in the journey, between 50 KB and 500 KB (50,000 to 500,000 bytes), spread across that range and including one of about 500 KB (450,000 to 500,000 bytes); the journey records each image's size and the analysis fails without a figure when the count or any size differs.
budgets.evidence: Manager's probe, 2026-10-06: one upload (HTTP 201, 0.8 s) plus one authenticated GET (200) per image; no spike.
budgets.command: Analysis of the telemetry the GitHub Projects (`onetaskgraph-github-projects-e2e`) domain's asset journeys record during its ordinary `test` target, reported through `onebudgetspec_core::report` by the command (or the one generic runner reading `ONEBUDGETSPEC_BUDGET_ID`) the convention lands in `otg-linear-budgets-domain`. It runs no journey and no `cargo test`, and it is cached on the domain tree, the measured production code and the onebudgetspec pin.

budgets.name: Duplicate
budgets.measure: Requests the github-projects plugin sends for one image on a re-copy, when the destination record's `onetaskgraph.assets` already records that image's sha256.
budgets.inner_measure_reason: As for github-asset-requests-per-new-asset: counted at a loopback endpoint because no check may reach the live board.
budgets.workload: The same document and task re-copied 3 times with unchanged images, then once with one image's bytes changed (that one counted against the new-asset budget instead). The images are those of the new-asset budget's workload, sized the same.
budgets.evidence: Design: the recorded `{sha256, url}` makes an unchanged image cost nothing; no spike.
budgets.command: Analysis of the telemetry the GitHub Projects (`onetaskgraph-github-projects-e2e`) domain's asset journeys record during its ordinary `test` target, reported through `onebudgetspec_core::report` by the command (or the one generic runner reading `ONEBUDGETSPEC_BUDGET_ID`) the convention lands in `otg-linear-budgets-domain`. It runs no journey and no `cargo test`, and it is cached on the domain tree, the measured production code and the onebudgetspec pin.

budgets.name: Punctuation: 1× / café — `literal`
budgets.measure: Requests the linear plugin sends for one image a copy carries that the destination record does not yet hold: the `fileUpload` mutation, the upload of the bytes to the URL it returns, and the authenticated read that verifies the asset URL.
budgets.inner_measure_reason: Headroom on a production Linear key every manager of a host shares is the measure of record and no check may reach it, so it is counted at the crate's loopback Linear workspace, as its existing budgets are.
budgets.workload: A document copy carrying 6 new images, and an issue copy carrying 2, into a linear source pointed at the loopback workspace. Each image is a PNG generated in the journey, between 50 KB and 500 KB (50,000 to 500,000 bytes), spread across that range and including one of about 500 KB (450,000 to 500,000 bytes); the journey records each image's size and the analysis fails without a figure when the count or any size differs.
budgets.evidence: Linear's documented upload flow is one mutation plus one PUT; one verifying GET mirrors the GitHub plugin's check; no spike.
budgets.command: Analysis of the telemetry the Linear (`onetaskgraph-linear-e2e`) domain's asset journeys record during its ordinary `test` target, reported through `onebudgetspec_core::report` by the command (or the one generic runner reading `ONEBUDGETSPEC_BUDGET_ID`) the convention lands in `otg-linear-budgets-domain`. It runs no journey and no `cargo test`, and it is cached on the domain tree, the measured production code and the onebudgetspec pin.
